instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Reveal the Truth in Layers
cards.instruction: Protect someone by disclosing the truth in stages, changing what each earlier statement appears to mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wedding venue has changed our booking. Sit with me a moment; I taught you to take one planning problem at a time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What changed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're asking before panicking this time. The date is still ours, but we can't use the building.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happened to the building?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fire. Nobody was hurt. We'll keep the date and find somewhere else together. You don't have to ring anyone yet; take that one thing at a time, as we practised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your garden gnome has come back from the exhibition. Sit here with me; you remember how I taught you to lay out a repair before starting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you brought it in a box?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're checking the packaging now. Good. It's in several pieces, wrapped separately so we can see what fits.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is all of it there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Most of it. The hat is missing, but the face is whole. Start with the smile, the way I showed you; I'll find the glue while you look at that bit.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I changed the meeting time. Did you change the room? I taught you to put every alteration on the same notice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You changed the time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, on the calendar, not the notice. You're checking the details now; good. That's my part of why nobody met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why didn't you tell me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I thought you'd object to an earlier start. Now give me your missing part, the way I taught you to complete a report: where did you send the others?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I hid the first complaint letter. Where did the second go? I taught you to keep every envelope with its date on it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've admitted hiding a letter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm putting it on the table. You've learnt to notice an omission; good. Now fill in the gap after mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There was a third letter, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll tell you where I kept the first: under the accounts. Put the other two beside it, in the order I taught you, and tell me which one you kept from me.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: It Was Foreshadowed
cards.instruction: Turn the failure into a planned turning point by returning to earlier details that now appear to predict it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The cake's collapse is the turn I planned. Remember that first wobble? I taught you to watch the layers before admiring the icing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You ignored the wobble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You noticed it yourself this time. I left it for you to see what came next. Get the bowl I asked you to keep empty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no cake left to put on a stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why I told you to keep the cream cold. We're making trifle now. Bring that empty bowl and layer the pieces as I showed you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tent coming down is where this lesson was heading. Remember the loose peg I pointed out? I taught you to check each corner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were supposed to hammer it in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered the tool at least. I left the peg loose so you'd see why that check matters. Now fetch the repair bag.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're standing in the rain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why I told you to pack waterproofs. This was always the wet-weather part. Put your hood up the way I showed you, then we'll practise securing the corner again.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I said the evening would flow, I meant this kitchen flood. I taught you to listen to the exact words before guessing what comes next.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You meant conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're remembering the conversation now. Good. And what are we all talking about? The water. You can give me that much.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't predict a burst pipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I said something would have to open up before the evening improved. Repeat the words carefully, as I taught you: 'open up'. What has that pipe just done?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My forecast said sunny. I meant your face when the refund arrived. I taught you to look at the whole trip, not just the weather.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The holiday was ruined by rain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've linked the cause to the result this time. No rain, no refund. That brighter ending is exactly what I told you to expect.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wrote 'pack sunscreen'.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the next trip we'd pay for with this refund. You used to read one line of my packing lists and stop. Keep the bottle; tell me I planned further ahead than you did.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Reverse the Score
cards.instruction: Turn each apparent loss into a new category of victory, then invite comparison on those changing terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last over the line, first at noticing the route. I taught you to look around when we ran; how many wildflowers did you see?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a speed contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You read the entry form this time. Good. Now name three things you passed. I can give you six before we reach the gate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I noticed the finish line. That's what counted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One thing against my six. Let's score memory instead; repeat my six after I say them, the way we practised on training runs. Ready to lose this round?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My small trophy shows restraint. I taught you to win without filling the room; put yours beside it and compare.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is the consolation prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can read an inscription now. Lovely. Can your huge cup fit in the cupboard without clearing a shelf? Mine can.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine says 'first'.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And mine doesn't need the announcement. Let's compare modesty. Put both on the mantelpiece, the way I taught you to display things; which one leaves room for anybody else?
